blocks.text: **Option D. It causes less release of histamine:** Cisatracurium is preferred over atracurium because it causes less release of histamine. Histamine release can lead to adverse effects such as bronchoconstriction, hypotension, and flushing. Cisatracurium is considered a non-histamine-releasing neuromuscular blocking agent, making it a favorable choice in patients who are susceptible to histamine-related reactions.

items.text: **Option A. It has rapid onset of action:** Cisatracurium and atracurium have similar onset of action. Both drugs are classified as intermediate-acting neuromuscular blocking agents and have comparable time to onset.

**Option B. It has less depressant action on the heart:** Cisatracurium and atracurium have similar cardiovascular effects. They do not have significant direct effects on the heart and do not cause substantial cardiovascular depression.

**Option C. It has a short duration of action:** Cisatracurium and atracurium have similar durations of action. The duration of effect for both drugs is moderate, allowing for adequate muscle relaxation during surgical procedures.

blocks.text: Naloxone sodium is used as an antidote for opioid poisoning cases. It is a competitive blockers of mu/kappa/delta receptors and produces lacrimation, mydriasis, salivation and increases respiration.
